text:
emily: heads-up — noticed steady memory growth on long-context batched runs (8k+ tokens). seems correlated with repeated reuse of small slabs. reproducer attached below.

emily: repro steps 
```bash
# run with 4 concurrent streams, long history
KV_DEBUG=1 python tools/repro_long_context.py --model rdx-7b --streams 4 --tokens 8192
# grab pprof after ~20 min
./tools/collect_pprof.sh pid
```

dave: can you paste the pprof top?

emily: pprof snapshot:
```
1.2GB  35.4%  runtime.kv_slab_alloc
800MB  23.6%  runtime.kv_lookup
400MB  11.8%  runtime.eviction_mark
```

ben: saw same pattern in a separate run. interestingly some entries have offsets that point 8 bytes before expected token boundary — looks like header drift.

carla: i dumped a couple of blocks, hex: 
```
block@0x7f9a3c00: header(0x10): 0x00 0x00 0x04 0x00 0xFF 0xEE 0x00 0x00 | payload: ...
expected token_idx 1024, found 1016
```

frank: preliminary theory: when a slab is evicted+reused we don't always rewrite the header tail. allocator reuses memory but the eviction path sometimes only updates length field, leaving a stale base index. cross-request contamination happens when a later request reads that stale base and reconstructs KV tags with wrong absolute positions.

emily: yep — i saw older request ids in current cache entries (request_id: 0x8f4c from 3 requests ago). that explains garbled attention for late tokens.

maria: proposed fixes:
- zero out slab metadata on eviction (cheap)
- add per-entry epoch tag (increment on each reuse)
- include a small header checksum to detect stale headers at read time
- assert alignment in debug builds (KV_ASSERT((ptr - slab_base) % ALIGN == 0))

dave: agree on epoch tag + assertions. also add a short fuzz test that rotates small slabs aggressively. i can own tests if someone opens a PR.

ben: quick patch i tested locally:
```
// mark slab as dead before reuse
slab->epoch = ++global_epoch;
memset(slab->meta_tail, 0, META_TAIL_SZ);
// verification on read
if (slab->checksum != calc_checksum(slab->meta)) { return MISS; }
```

carla: repro with env var KV_DEBUG=1 yields this snippet from logs: 
```
[KV][WARN] slab 0x7f9a3c00 header checksum mismatch, dropping entry (epoch 42 -> 43)
[KV][INFO] reuse count=12 frag=0.23
```

emily: perfect — i'll open a PR with epoch+zeroing+asserts and a unit test that simulates rotating reuse under high concurrency. will also add the checksum fallback to avoid silent contamination. :thumbsup:

dev-bot: created issue #4821: "kv-slab-header-drift -> cross-request contamination" and linked to CI job kv/fuzz/rotation.

frank: long-term: consider switching to power-of-two slab sizes to reduce misalignment edge cases, and revisit the batching heuristics that encourage tiny allocations.

maria: also let's run a canary against dedicated runtime next week. minimal risk change but we should monitor latency and tail mem use.

emily: noted. i'll include perf regression test (end-to-end with 16 concurrent streams) in the PR. if all green we'll roll canary -> staged -> prod.

dave: thanks everyone. created a follow-up card to track post-merge checks (kv-epoch-metrics, header-failure-rate).

emily: thanks — will update here when PR is up and when canary runs.
